title: 20 CFR Part 639 - Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification
date_evidence: Displaying title 20, up to date as of 10/23/2026. Title 20 was last amended 10/19/2026.
key_claim: The US WARN regulation requires 60 days' notice of a plant closing or mass layoff and defines employment loss as an employment termination other than a discharge for cause, voluntary departure, or retirement.
frame_summary: The regulation defines what triggers US layoff notice, and its definition of employment loss excludes voluntary departure and retirement.
verbatim_quote: an employment termination, other than a discharge for cause, voluntary departure, or retirement
verbatim_list: WARN requires employers who are planning a plant closing or a mass layoff to give affected employees at least 60 days' notice of such an employment action.

title: When you must consult: Collective consultation for redundancy
date_evidence: Evergreen guidance page, accessed 2026-10-31; page shows Last updated 07 April 2026
key_claim: Acas states that collective consultation is required where 20 or more redundancies are proposed at one establishment within 90 days, that voluntary redundancies must be counted, and that redundancies must not be staggered to avoid consultation.
frame_summary: Acas explains when UK employers must consult collectively on redundancy, including that voluntary redundancies count toward the threshold.
verbatim_quote: You should not stagger redundancies to avoid consultation.
verbatim_list: By law, you must hold collective consultation where all of the following apply: you're proposing 20 or more redundancies; the redundancies are in one establishment – not necessarily in your organisation as a whole, which may be much larger; you propose to make the redundancies within a 90-day period

When counting how many employees could be made redundant, you must include: voluntary redundancies – for example if you propose to make 22 employees redundant but 6 of them volunteer for redundancy, you must still collectively consult

You must do this before you issue any individual notice of dismissal, and at least: 30 days before the first dismissal, if there are between 20 and 99 redundancies; 45 days before the first dismissal, if there are 100 or more redundancies
notes: Public body guidance, last updated 07/04/2026 (more than six months before the scan date), so cited as an evergreen reference page, not as a recency anchor.

title: Redundancy: your rights: Consultation
key_claim: GOV.UK states that where an employer is making 20 or more redundancies at the same time the collective redundancy rules apply, and that employees can claim at a tribunal if the employer does not consult properly.
frame_summary: GOV.UK sets out the UK employee-facing rule that 20 or more redundancies at the same time trigger collective consultation.
verbatim_quote: If they’re making 20 or more redundancies at the same time, the collective redundancy rules apply.
verbatim_list: You can make a claim to an employment tribunal if your employer does not consult properly, for example if they start late, or do not consult at all.
notes: Date is the page's updated-at metadata; first published 2012-01-25. The page does not mention voluntary redundancy; that point rests on Acas.

title: Job Cuts Fall in September; Hiring Plans Up 3% Over 2025 On Weak Early Seasonal Hiring
key_claim: Challenger counted 43,281 announced US job cuts in September 2026, and AI has been cited in 120,136 announcements this year, about 21% of all cuts and the leading reason year to date.
frame_summary: Challenger reports announced US job cuts falling in 2026 while AI remains the most-cited reason year to date.
verbatim_quote: So far this year, AI has been cited in 120,136 job cut announcements, approximately 21% of all cuts, and it remains the leading reason year-to-date.
verbatim_list: Through September, employers have announced 573,195 job cuts, down 39% from the 946,426 cuts announced in the first nine months of 2025.
U.S.-based employers announced 43,281 job cuts in September, down 18% from the 52,881 announced in August.
notes: Challenger counts announced job cuts; the article does not discuss voluntary exits or Microsoft.

title: Microsoft offers buyouts to around 60,000 employees
key_claim: Microsoft confirmed buyouts to around 60,000 employees in the US, Canada, India and the UK, on terms similar to standard severance; an earlier offer to roughly 8,750 retirement-age staff drew acceptance from more than 30%.
frame_summary: TechCrunch reports the buyout as a way for Microsoft to cut headcount without mass layoffs.
verbatim_quote: The buyout offer gives Microsoft a way to reduce its workforce without resorting to the more disruptive approach of mass layoffs.
verbatim_list: Earlier this year, Microsoft offered buyouts to retirement-age employees, with more than 30% of the roughly 8,750 eligible workers accepting.
Employees at the vice president level and below on select teams in the United States, Canada, India, and the United Kingdom will be eligible, according to the note.
The terms of the buyout will be similar to Microsoft’s standard severance.
notes: Updated 26/10/2026 11:21 AM PT with details from Microsoft. WARN and consultation law not mentioned.

title: Microsoft Opens Voluntary Exits to Copilot and AI Teams
key_claim: UC Today relays that staff have until early December to decide and that those who accept will leave on 31 December, with no age or tenure requirement and performance not a factor.
